findings.claim: A subgradient at a zero L1 coordinate may be any value in [-1,1], so primal support does not force dual support. The continuum sketch makes the same invalid inference.

The K2 disjoint-union K2 and P6 necessity examples use arbitrary nonnegative potentials, but these forests have zero quotient and therefore zero minimal residual under A1-A2. Moreover a one-vertex positive load cannot equal the sum of absolute incident edge residuals. These examples support necessity in the enlarged arbitrary-potential theorem only, not the original defect-derived class.

The final open-problem setup says aggregation preserves total defect although its proved hypothesis gives a non-increase, and treats a static dual capacity bound as a propagation rate without a dynamics. Those premises do not follow from the proved static results.
